translation.title: Ibuprofen Plaster
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief of osteoarthritis (degenerative arthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, epicondylitis of the humerus (such as tennis elbow), muscle pain, and swelling and pain after an injury.
translation.usage: Peel off the release liner and apply it to the affected area once a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it (asthma, allergic rhinitis, rash), if you are hypersensitive to or have experienced hypersensitivity (bronchospasm, angioedema) to aspirin, other analgesics, or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, if you have or have had bronchial asthma, if you have or have had gastrointestinal bleeding, if you have a gastric or duodenal ulcer, if you have had a peptic ulcer, if you have severe heart failure or severe kidney or liver impairment, if the user is a child aged 12 years or under, or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy or breastfeeding. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are elderly, if you have chronic bronchitis, allergic rhinitis, or inflammation of the nasal mucosa, if you have had a gastrointestinal disorder (such as gastrointestinal ulcer, bleeding or perforation, ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease), if you have liver or kidney impairment or heart failure, if you have had high blood pressure or kidney disease, if you are pregnant (first or second trimester) or planning a pregnancy, if you have developed intolerance after taking aspirin or ibuprofen, if you have experienced allergic symptoms to a medicine (rash, redness, itching, dermatitis), if you have an allergic constitution, if your skin is very moist or eroded, or if you have a circulatory disorder or diabetes. Follow the prescribed directions and dosage. Use this medicine externally only and do not take it by mouth. Do not use it on or around the eyes or on mucous membranes, and take care that it does not get into the eyes. Do not use an occlusive dressing. Do not use it together with aspirin or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics. Rash, redness, itching, flushing, stinging pain, skin rash, skin exfoliation, dry skin, abscess or pustule formation, hives, a burning sensation, aseptic meningitis with symptoms such as headache, nausea, vomiting, fever, a stiff neck or clouded consciousness, dry mouth, altered taste, facial swelling, small blisters, eosinophilia, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, general malaise, mild redness or slight irritation at the application site, scaling, and rarely shock, eczema, dermatitis, contact dermatitis, erythema, oedema, and very rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome, erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, toxic epidermal necrolysis, photosensitivity, or local hypersensitivity may occur. If any of these occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature away from moisture and light, and keep out of reach of children.
